text:
alex: FYI nightly eval flagged a regression after the pset v26 rebaseline we merged last night. failures up ~6% on intent extraction. eval-bot: nightly-summary: pset-v26 | baseline-failures=118 | today=125 | delta=+7

maya: ugh — can you paste a failing example?

alex: pasted one below. seems like several cases where the model drops slot values when we removed two anchor examples from the promptset.

alex: ```
SYSTEM: You are an assistant that extracts intents and slots.
FEW_SHOT: [examples reduced — removed anchor examples for refund/cancellation]
INPUT: "I need to cancel my subscription and get a refund for last month."
MODEL_OUTPUT: "cancel_subscription"
EXPECTED: {"intent":"cancel_subscription","refund":true}
```

liam: hmm, removing anchor examples could change the probability mass on the multi-turn cue. Do we have tokenization/truncation diffs from the rebaseline script?

sophia: I ran a quick diff between old_promptset.txt and new_promptset.txt — the trimming moved an anchor that used to be right before the user example. That anchor had a short explicit refund example. Without it, the label distribution shifts.

maya: could quantization play a role? this is only on nightly eval which uses quantized candidate model for cost reasons.

alex: good call. the failing cases are mainly from the quantized runner. on CPU quantized inference we see shorter completions. example above loses the boolean slot.

liam: steps: 1) revert promptset trim in a canary branch and re-run nightly on quantized runner, 2) run the same promptset against fp16 hosted model to check if purely quantization, 3) add targeted canary tests for refund/cancel anchors.

jen: +1 to targeted canary. we need a quick decision — revert rebaseline for tomorrow's run or push a hotfix that reintroduces the anchor example. ops: what is the rollback cost?

alex: rollback is low — it's a promptset rebaseline commit. I can open PR to reintroduce one anchor and mark as canary.

eval-bot: nightly-run: queued re-run (canary) on quantized runner at 2134001300. will post results.

maya: thanks. once we have canary results post them here. if quantization is the root cause we should add a note to the onboarding checklist: "verify critical anchors survive prompt compression/quantized token budgets."

liam: also add a small unit test that asserts slot presence for a handful of anchor inputs. saved us before. :+1:

alex: opening PR now -> link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/pset/compare/pset-v26-restore-anchor. will tag @maya @liam for quick review.

sophia: copy. will run a diff eval between fp16 and quantized on the canary outputs and report mismatches.

eval-bot: canary-run completed: quantized canary failures decreased from 125 -> 119 (partial improvement). full diff pending.

alex: partial improvement suggests anchor helps but still some residual delta. follow-up: check tokenizer boundary changes in rebaseline pipeline and add a failing-case harness to nightly.

jen: good triage. keep me posted if we need to freeze rebaselines for next week.

maya: thanks everyone — strong action items.
